correctness.rationale: For every squarefree degree-m companion matrix C and any finite field, J is invertible, S=diag(C,C^T) is J-self-adjoint, and ad rank <=1 iff the noncentral vector is an eigenvector. After algebraic closure, S has m two-dimensional eigenspaces. Its minors generate the intersection of m coordinate primes, establishing scheme reducedness. Localizations and quadratic tangent equations determine singular locus and Hilbert series. Frobenius roots then give exact all-extension counts and the rational zeta and Möbius-recovery formulas. Exact finite-field direct-rank code verified eight split/nonsplit cases, but infinite claims rest on proofs.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Earlier normal-form results can imply the existence of a spectral decomposition. They do not by themselves assert or enumerate the reduced intersection-of-primes scheme or derive Frobenius point counts. A new argument from determinant ideals and Frobenius action is required for this single combined theorem; it is provided. Some standard ingredients themselves are known and are not claimed as new.

Published mathematical-record matches on adjoint ranks concern other Lie classes. The comparison distinguishes logical implications and recognizes residual unsearched specialized literature; it does not infer uniqueness from missing matches.

value.rationale: The natural regular centre-two two-step Lie family has a complete rank-one centralizer scheme and uniform arithmetic zeta classification. A geometric invariant encodes each finite-field irreducible-factor degree of its Pfaffian, supplying a motivated exact invariant rather than a small numerical slice. The result distinguishes geometric and rational centralizer stratifications across all dimensions, including characteristic two.
